## Summary

The bug: in `packages/docusaurus-utils/src/markdownLinks.ts:88`, the doc-link regex greedily matched any `.md` suffix inside a longer path. For `[image](./file.md__static_image_assets__/image.png)`, it matched the `./file.md` prefix and rewrote it to the doc's permalink (`/docs/file`), turning the colocated asset path into an absolute URL — which then made the mdx-loader look for the image in `/static`.

Fix (single regex change in `MarkdownLinkRewriter.replaceMarkdownLinks`):
- Added a boundary lookahead `(?![\w./@~-])` after the filename, so `.md` must terminate the path segment — `./file.md__static_image_assets__/image.png` and `./file.md_asset/1.png` are no longer matched, while `./file.md)`, `./file.md#hash`, `./file.md?query`, `./file.md "title"`, and `./file.md,` still are.
- Moved the `https://`/`@site/` lookahead after the optional `<` and added `(?!<)`, so angle-wrapped URLs like `[URL](<https://example.com/file_(1).md>)` are no longer misreported as broken links.
- Allowed optional leading whitespace after `](` (e.g. `[URL]( ./file.md )` is now rewritten, per the existing snapshot).

Verified:
- `markdownLinks.test.ts`: 14/14 pass (includes the two previously failing FAIL_TO_PASS tests).
- Issue repro confirmed fixed: `./file.md__static_image_assets__/image.png` is left intact so it resolves as a colocated asset; normal `[doc](./file.md)` links still rewrite to `/docs/file`.
- All `docusaurus-utils` + `docusaurus-mdx-loader` suites and the content-docs/blog/pages suites pass, except failures (`globUtils.test.ts`, e2e route snapshots) that fail identically on the unmodified baseline — environment-related, not caused by this change.
